## 1. General description of the product with digital elements

### 1.1 Intended purpose — Annex VII(1)(a)

A self-hosted payment reconciliation gateway. It is deployed by financial institutions inside their own network, exposes an HTTPS API to internal systems and connects outbound to clearing providers. It is not intended for direct exposure to the public internet.

| CRA product category | Important product, class I (Annex III, class I) |

### 1.3 Description

Distributed as a signed OCI image plus a Helm chart. Ships a Go API service, a bundled administrative web UI and a Java plugin runtime that hosts the clearing adapters written for each institution.

## 2. Design, development, production and vulnerability handling processes

### 2.1 Design and development — Annex VII(2)(a)

Trunk-based development with mandatory two-reviewer pull requests. Every merge runs unit tests, static analysis, dependency scanning and an SBOM build. Release artefacts are built on ephemeral CI runners from a tagged commit and signed before publication. Threat modelling is repeated whenever an externally reachable interface changes.

**Production and release process**

**TODO — set `processes.production` in the product profile.**

### 2.2 Vulnerability handling — Annex VII(2)(b), Annex I Part II

Dependency scans run on every merge and nightly against the released tags still in support. Findings are triaged within two business days; critical findings reachable from an external interface are patched in a hotfix release within seven calendar days. Every triage decision is recorded as an OpenVEX statement published alongside the release.

**Security update policy**

Security fixes are released as separate patch versions that contain no functional change, are published to the same OCI registry and Helm repository as functional releases, and are announced through the security advisory feed. Updates are free of charge for the whole support period.

**Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy** — https://www.example.com/security/disclosure-policy

**SBOM publication** — A CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM is attached to every GitHub release and published as an OCI referrer next to the image digest.

## 3. Cybersecurity risk assessment — Annex VII(3), Article 13(2)

The gateway holds credentials for clearing providers and processes transaction data on behalf of the deploying institution. The dominant risks are credential compromise on the outbound connections, tampering with reconciliation results, and denial of service against the transaction API.

Assessment date: 2026-06-12

**Assets**

- Clearing provider API credentials held in the gateway keystore
- Transaction and reconciliation records at rest
- The administrative session of an operator

**Threats considered**

- Credential extraction from a compromised container filesystem
- Tampering with reconciliation output through an unauthenticated internal caller
- Resource exhaustion of the transaction API by a misbehaving internal client

**Mitigations**

- Keystore sealed with a deployment-scoped KMS key, never written to logs
- Mutual TLS required on every internal API caller
- Per-client rate limiting and bounded request body size on all endpoints
